engine.meaning: All steps and code kept: the _projects_ directory, the commands, _main.rs_, Listing 1-1, `.\main` on Windows. The link label is altered to "[“Troubleshootin'”][troubleshooting]", which changes visible link text but not the target.
engine.sense: Little slang to carry sense; "make a brand-spankin'-new source file" overstates "a new source file" but fits.
engine.authenticity: Eye dialect bolted onto the original prose: "makin' a directory to store yer Rust code", "a _projects_ directory'n a directory", "compile'n run the file". No Australian idiom, just dropped letters.
engine.register: Far lighter than level 5: the prose is the original's with dropped g's, e.g. "Rust files always end with the _.rs_ extension." No swearing.
engine.tone: The friendly tutorial tone survives, cluttered by spellings inside technical lines: "Regardless of your operatin' system".
engine.flow: Clunky contractions: "the _main.rs_ file ya just created'n enter the code", "enter the followin' commands to compile'n run the file".
engine.essence: Recognisably the Rust book page, as it is mostly the original.

yarn.meaning: Every step and code block kept: the _projects_ directory, the commands, _main.rs_, the underscore convention, `.\main` on Windows, the troubleshooting pointer.
yarn.sense: Terms fit: "Rust couldn’t care less where your code lives", "punch in the code", "have a squiz back at the [“Troubleshooting”]", "good on ya!", "welcome aboard!".
yarn.authenticity: Natural: "You’ll kick off by making a directory", "head back to your terminal window", "we reckon you should make a _projects_ directory".
yarn.register: A friendly middle weight, nearer level 3 than the full level 5: many lines stay plain, such as "Open a terminal and enter the following commands". No swearing.
yarn.tone: Keeps the warm, encouraging tutorial tone: "That makes you a Rust programmer—welcome aboard!"
yarn.flow: Reads like it was written that way: "So, use _hello_world.rs_, not _helloworld.rs_."
yarn.variety: Varied: "kick off", "couldn’t care less", "punch in", "head back", "have a squiz", "good on ya".
yarn.essence: Unmistakably the Rust book page, retold.

unharnessed.meaning: Every step and code block kept. "we reckon you make a _projects_ directory" drops the "should" of the suggestion; additions like "you bloody legend!" are colour on the congratulations.
unharnessed.sense: Mostly fits: "Rust couldn't give a toss where your code lives", "the done thing is to stick an underscore between 'em", "Fire up a terminal", "ways to get a hand". "chuck in this" for entering commands strains a little.
unharnessed.authenticity: Sounds like an Aussie dev talking: "First up", "the done thing", "good on ya, you bloody legend!". "we reckon you make a _projects_ directory" is ungrammatical.
unharnessed.register: A full, broad voice through the prose, close to level 5, with "bloody" and "give a toss" well within uncle-bob.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the encouraging tutorial tone, amplified: "Welcome aboard, mate!"
